title: Study: Emotions, Creativity Tightly Linked

image.attribution: User:Gryffindor and User:Megodenas / Wikimedia Commons / CC-BY-SA-3.0

main_content:
Music can evoke all sorts of emotions in listeners’ hearts, and in composers’ minds.

Brain-scanning studies of artists being creative – improvising music, rapping or drawing caricatures - showed deactivation in a part of the brain involved in planning and monitoring behavior.

Researchers say this is a sign of the “flow state” that frees up creative impulses.

A new study of jazz pianists shows a greater deactivation in that region when they are working on melodies to convey a happy emotion, rather than expressing a sad or negative emotion.

Improvising somber music activates the brain’s reward regions, which reinforce behaviors that lead to pleasurable outcomes. That could mean “that people are getting into more of a ‘groove,'” according to Malinda McPherson, who led the study. “This indicates there may be different mechanisms for why it’s pleasurable to create happy versus sad music.”  “The bottom line is that emotion matters,” says senior author Charles Limb.

The study of the neural intricacies of creativity was published in Scientific Reports.

questions.question: What can music do to listeners and composers?
options: Evoke emotions in listeners’ hearts and composers’ minds
Guarantee creative success in every artist
questions.answer: Evoke emotions in listeners’ hearts and composers’ minds

questions.question: What have brain-scanning studies on artists shown?
options: Increased activity in brain regions used for planning and behavior monitoring
Deactivation in regions of the brain related to planning and behavior monitoring
No measurable brain changes during creative work
Activation only in the brain's language centers
questions.answer: Deactivation in regions of the brain related to planning and behavior monitoring

questions.question: What does this “flow state” help achieve?
options: It prevents artists from making mistakes
It forces artists to follow a strict plan
It reduces the need for musical training
